slides.headline: Cybercab Just Gave a Blind Man His Independence Back
slides.body: Gary Moss lost his sight 5 years ago. He rode a Cybercab in Austin, talked to Grok mid-ride, and said: 'Other people's driving scares me, but these cars don't.' He praised the legroom and called it a glimpse of getting his independence back

slides.headline: Cybercab Sets the All-Time Efficiency Record for Any Production Car
slides.body: The car gets over 6.1 miles per kWh, the best efficiency number any production vehicle has ever recorded. One rider put in a full 5 hours across Austin and came back talking about the numbers. 'Still can't believe this thing is real,' he said

slides.headline: SpaceX Just Crossed 600 Autonomous Rocket Landings
slides.body: Six hundred times, a SpaceX booster has launched and guided itself back to the exact pad it left from, no human hand on the controls. The count crossed 600 this week. You probably missed the 599th

slides.headline: Trump: 'Whoever Wins AI, Wins'
slides.body: Donald Trump said it flat out: 'Whoever wins AI, wins.' He called it bigger than the internet and a full revolution. The US has framed this race as the thing that determines the future

slides.headline: Judge Rules: Americans Have No Right to Accurate Information from Officials
slides.body: A US federal judge ruled this week that the Constitution does not guarantee a right to accurate information from public officials. The same ruling covers clean drinking water. Both were argued in court, neither holds up as a constitutional guarantee

slides.headline: SAVE TODAY'S AI BRIEFING
slides.body:
Cybercab gave a blind man his independence back in Austin
Cybercab posted the all-time production car efficiency record, 6.1 mi/kWh
SpaceX crossed 600 autonomous landings
Trump: 'Whoever wins AI, wins'
US court: no constitutional right to accurate information

caption:

A blind man rode Tesla's Cybercab in Austin and said it gave him his independence back, Cybercab set the all-time production car efficiency record at 6.1 miles per kWh, SpaceX crossed 600 autonomous rocket landings, Trump said 'whoever wins AI wins' and called it bigger than the internet, a US court ruled there is no constitutional right to accurate information from public officials.

Autonomous vehicles are no longer promises, people are logging hours in them now. The AI race just got a clear geopolitical frame.
